consulted_citations.field: 四 entry, graphic history and attributed analyses; PDF p. 1279, printed p. 1264, continued PDF p. 1280, printed p. 1265
consulted_citations.text: The actual headword is 四 in 四部. I inspected both supplied full-page scan images directly. On printed p. 1264, the entry describes Shang forms as four accumulated strokes used directly for the numeral, normalized as 亖, and says they continued alongside forms written 四 in bronze inscriptions from Western Zhou through Han. It dates a separate graph series to Spring and Autumn and reports Shuowen’s ‘image of division into four’ analysis. The continuation on printed p. 1265 attributes to Ma Xulun the proposal that 四 was the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; the book explicitly says the proposal lacks textual attestation. This is a reported proposal, not an established derivation. The inspected passage names 泗, not 呬. The quoted relevant OCR passage agrees with the pixels; no OCR correction is proposed.
